analysis.title: SPX Upside / US CPI Ahead / Nvidia / Japan Households / China Outlook
key_insights: UBS structuring strategist Rebecca Cheong expects SPX to rise at least 10% over the next three months in a lower-volatility rally. She cites washed-out systematic positioning and little remaining systematic selling.

Risk Control exposure is 55%, the lowest since the tariff episode. The two prior comparable washouts were 55% on Aug. 6, 2024 and 30% on April 10, 2025, after which SPX rose 17% and 24% over four months.
CTA equity exposure is -5%. UBS says negative CTA exposure has historically been a bottoming signal, especially when real-money investors are not selling.
Real-money support from retail, foreign investors and corporate buybacks (returning next week) should keep news-driven selloffs shallow. Short-squeeze risk and CTA/Risk Control re-risking add upside.

October CPI is due Tuesday and is the last CPI the Fed sees before the Dec. 8-9 FOMC. Alan Detmeister expects headline 0.26% m/m vs 0.29% consensus and 0.32% UBS Nowcast, and core 0.23% vs 0.24% consensus and 0.22% Nowcast.

Lower gasoline prices should hold headline CPI down and falling used vehicle prices should weigh on core. PPI is due Friday, with bond markets closed Wednesday for Veterans Day. UBS warns against leaning on October PCE estimates until PPI is in.

Nvidia fell 5.5% Monday on China-related news and drove most single-stock inbound to the desk. Investors mostly expect the issue to blow over, and the earnings bar looks intact with a January-quarter revenue expectation near $135bn.

The desk's best estimate is that Nvidia's China exposure is concentrated in a portion of Singapore revenue, where assemblers may serve Chinese companies. The debate also covers what Washington wants from Nvidia, including possible US foundry investment.

Karl Keirstead (UBS Equity Research) says the market is too bearish on political risk to AI data center buildout. Debate centers on tightening permitting, not stopping projects under construction, so the larger impact would fall on 2028+ capacity.

Timothy Arcuri says the SOX's roughly 30% drop over the past month, including about 12% last week after the midterms, prices in roughly 30% and 35% cuts to Street CY2027 and CY2028 EPS. That implies about 55GW of CY2028 shipments vs 70GW originally expected, against about 50GW of high-confidence powered-shell capacity.

Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei called reports of US talks 'fake news' and demanded acceptance of seven conditions. Iran says normal Hormuz traffic will not resume until they are met, contrasting with Trump's 'positive momentum' view.

CTA flows are rotating out of tech and duration shorts and into Europe and credit. Nasdaq momentum flipped short, simulations show $40bn of equity selling at 7,200 and positive flows only near 7,900, and CTAs have roughly halved US10y and EU10y shorts.

Japan September household spending fell 6.8% y/y vs a 3.1% decline expected, the largest drop since September 2020. Some BoJ policymakers want faster hikes, the BoJ is at 1.25%, and a December hike is widely expected.
UBS China Economics (Yu Song) expects about 4.6% GDP growth in 2027, a 4.5-5% target again, a smaller net export contribution and further RMB appreciation.
UBS desk views a GBP 5s10s30s receive trade at about -12.5bp targeting -17bp, and favours payers in December/February MPC pricing at 16-22bp, after the MPC's 8-1 hawkish vote.

UK October BRC retail sales rose 1.5% y/y and Barclays card spending rose 2.3% y/y, with fuel spending up 22.7%. Australian Westpac consumer sentiment fell to 78.2, the lowest since late 2022, after an RBA 25bp hike.
UBS Economics (George Tharenou) forecasts Australian GDP growth of 1.4% in 2027 and headline CPI of 4.5% in Q4 2026, keeping the RBA restrictive.

S&P 500 implied vol fell sharply Monday, with the front-end straddle going home at 75bp ahead of CPI. Investors sold November expiry protection and bought VIX put spreads and put ratios, and skew normalised while the term structure steepened.
The US 3y auction tailed 0.4bp and was issued about 30bp richer than October's. USTs caught a late bid on Hegseth impeachment and Iran deal headlines that faded into the close.

market_movers.rationale: Stock fell 5.5% Monday on China-related news. Desk sees China exposure concentrated in part of Singapore revenue, and investors still hold a January-quarter revenue expectation near $135bn.

sector_views.rationale: UBS Equity Research (Arcuri) says the SOX selloff already prices much of the data-center power constraint, while desk flows show long-only selling into strength in AI and semiconductor names.
Networking, optical and power infrastructure were better sponsored than semiconductors and compute in Monday's rotation within AI.

earnings_insights: Nvidia: investors have not backed away from a January-quarter revenue expectation closer to $135bn (expectation, not reported). Earnings are approaching.
Japan reports due Tuesday: Fujikura, Honda, SoftBank, Toray and Subaru. Kikkoman (-12.4%) and Ajinomoto (-6.5%) fell on earnings.
Arcuri's implied cuts: current SOX prices imply roughly 30% lower Street CY2027 EPS and 35% lower CY2028 EPS, about 20% lower implied CY2028 revenue (UBS analysis, not reported figures).

vol_and_positioning: Risk Control exposure at 55% is the lowest since the tariff episode, and CTA equity exposure is -5%. UBS says the downside systematic feedback loop has largely been removed.
CTA simulations show $40bn of equity selling at SPX 7,200 and positive flows only near 7,900. Nasdaq momentum has flipped short.
CTAs roughly halved US10y and EU10y short positions but remain broadly short. They remain long USD and short most G10 and Asian currencies.
S&P 500 implied vol collapsed again Monday, with front-end vol falling sharply and the straddle going home at 75bp ahead of CPI.
Investors dumped protection, mostly in November regular expiry, and bought VIX put spreads and put ratios. Skew normalised from stretched levels and the term structure steepened.
Long-only investors were selective sellers into strength in better-owned AI and semiconductor names. Cash desk flows showed shorts covering.
Japan equity flows were 50% better to sell.
geopolitical: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei rejected US reports of negotiations and demanded acceptance of seven conditions conveyed through Qatar in September, including ending the war on all fronts, releasing frozen funds and lifting the US naval blockade.
Iran says normal Hormuz traffic will not resume until its conditions are met. Trump has assessed that renewed US military action looks unlikely.
Nvidia's China access, Washington's push for greater US investment including domestic foundry capacity, and political risk around US data center permitting.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's impeachment headlines and a potential Iran deal briefly moved USTs.
